content.intro: In this lesson, you will study bootstrap with npm and version control and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Bootstrap with npm and Version Control is part of a reproducible delivery workflow. Pin versions, keep source files distinct from generated output, confirm licensing and asset paths, and inspect the built artifacts rather than relying only on a development preview.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating bootstrap with npm and version control as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
